summary: Rajat Verma works in the computational field and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.
Rajeev Kinra is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (1999–2008). He became an Associate Professor at Northwestern University in 2007.

Rajeev Kumar is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University and Panjab University (PhD 2013), and has held posts at Panjab University and the University of Delhi.

Rajeev Sangal is a computational linguist and Indologist who studied at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania. His career includes posts at IIT Kanpur (1982–1998), IIT (BHU) Varanasi (2013–2018), and IIIT Hyderabad (2002–2013, 2018–2022).

Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Sushil Kumar De. He held posts at Jagannath University, the University of Dhaka (1939–1951), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendrakumar Dabee specializes in philosophy and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Madras after degrees from several institutions. He worked at the Ministry of Education (1993–2013) and became Senior Lecturer at Mahatma Gandhi Institute in 2013.

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Hindu School, Calcutta Medical College, and the University of Calcutta. He served at The Asiatic Society, was director of Wards' Institution (1856–1881), and founded Sarasvat Samaj.

Rajesh P. N. Rao is a computational and Indology scholar who studied at Angelo State University and the University of Rochester under Dana H. Ballard. In 2000, he became a Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University. He held academic posts at Presidency University and Scottish Church College.

Raju Rimal is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus, Tribhuvan University, and the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (PhD). He has held research and academic posts at NMBU, the University of Oslo, and NIH.

Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under John Marshall. He held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Trijang Rinpoche as well as under Gendun Chopel from circa 1946 to 1951.

Ralf Kramer is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London. He has served as a Tibetan librarian at Oxford's Indian Institute and the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) worked in philosophy and other fields, earning degrees at the University of Michigan and studying under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, Princeton, and the University of California, Santa Cruz (1968–).
Ralph Lerner is a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Chicago (circa 1945–1953) under Leo Strauss. He subsequently held a post at the University of Chicago from circa 1953 to 2003.

Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge. He held positions at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Banaras Hindu University, and served as Director of SOAS University of London (1922–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit, headmaster at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, and principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Ralph Waldo Emerson (1803–1882) was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He completed his studies at Harvard College, Harvard University (circa 1817–1821), and Harvard Divinity School (circa 1825–1826).

Raluwe Padmasiri is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Padmasiri became a Professor at the University of Kelaniya in 2012 and holds a professorship attested at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.
Ram Chandra Dhungana is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who served as an Assistant Editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).
